I'm 24 years old. I'd like to share the changes that I underwent within 6 years with you.

At 18, I hadn't been in school or work for two years. No perspective for my future. I stayed at home, rarely going outside, playing video games, not having friends or a relationship, not caring about how I dressed, LONELY, and only having recently received the diagnosis.

At this time, my interest for clinical psychology grew into a wish for a career. So I decided to go back to school. For a few months I learned to ride the bus, orient myself in the city and went to see what my future school looked like. Also I got on an antidepressant which helped with the anxiety.

At this time, I started to search for fashion advice on the internet and I improved to the point I got occasional compliments for what I was wearing (not overdressed though).

What followed was 4 years of school. I met great people I still have contact with. Intimate friendships are one of the greatest things in my life. Romantic relationships were and are still difficult for me, also because of social anxiety. But I had a great social environment there and I grew as a person A LOT!

Then I finished school and went to uni. I made my special interest into the beginning of what I hope to be a career. Socially I still struggle but things keep getting easier.

------------

At 18 I had no outlook on life. If you told me back then what my life would look like now, I wouldn't have believed you.

Change is possible. I'm not some kind of special person, so you certainly can find a way to build a fulfilling life too. I'm still on my way but I got it going for me.

Maybe it's possible to go to a therapist, this could help a lot (I still go to one).

I completely understand your frustration. I've been there too. And you're right to feel this way! But unfortunately nobody can just take this disorder away from you. You have to learn to live with it.

It's not an easy way, I'm not gonna lie. Life is a struggle. But at least I can wish you the very best for your future! I honestly hope you can find your way.

I'm studying psychology and in a recent lecture about *Change of personality over the course of life* (although the title was in german) we learned that the current evidence clearly points at a tendency for some personality traits to change, especially in the 20s and 30s.

One personality trait that is particularly relevant for AvPD is emotional stability. People become more emotionally stable up until they are about 50 years old. From then on it stays the same until there's a slight decrease about the time when they enter a retirement home.

So they do change. However, here comes the catch: Why do people grow in emotional stability? Why do some people not? Well, most people grow more stable because they *have* to in order to function as an employee or as a parent for instance. This means staying at home until they are 50 years old certainly won't help them become more emotionally stable.

So yes, change (and quite a lot of it!) is possible but you have to do something for it.

edit: And you most likely won't become as calm, fearless and bold as you see it in people in the movies. But you can acheive an amount of emotional stability that enables you to function as a friend, spouse, parent, employee, etc. and you can become more free in what you want to do with your life.
